newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. Customs team in HK to check textile exports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Customs team in HK to check textile exports.

text.p: The U.S. Customs Service has sent a delegation to Hong Kong to evaluate the effectiveness of efforts to detect and prevent illegal transshipments of textile products, the U.S. consulate general said on Thursday.

The delegation's findings would be one factor in the U.S. Customs' expected review of additional import requirements imposed on some categories of Hong Kong textiles last year, it said in a statement.

The team's visit, to be concluded in early February, is part of an ongoing cooperative effort with the Hong Kong government, and will continue the work of a group that visited the territory last September, the statement said.
The team will observe Hong Kong authorities who are enforcing rules against export to the United States of textiles mislabelled as having been manufactured in Hong Kong, it said.
The Hong Kong government said last month it would allow U.S. officials to join its customs officers on inspections of the territory's textiles factories in a bid to resolve their trade row.
Washington says manufacturers in China are dodging quota limits by sewing on false "Made in Hong Kong" labels.

U.S. Customs last June imposed rules requiring Hong Kong textile exporters to provide additional import documentation on a number of products in an attempt to stop illegal transshipments passing from China through Hong Kong to the United States.
